questions.enonce_markdown: The sum of the first and second terms of a geometric progression is $-5$ while the sum of the fourth and fifth terms of the same progression is $40$. Find the first term and common ratio of the progression. (6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let the first term be $a$ and the common ratio $r$. The $n$th term is $ar^{n-1}$.

First and second terms: $a + ar = a(1 + r) = -5$. (1)

Fourth and fifth terms: $ar^3 + ar^4 = ar^3(1 + r) = 40$. (2)

From (1), $1 + r \neq 0$, so we may divide (2) by (1):

$$\frac{ar^3(1+r)}{a(1+r)} = \frac{40}{-5} \;\Longrightarrow\; r^3 = -8 \;\Longrightarrow\; r = -2$$

($r$ is real, and $r^3 = -8$ has the single real root $-2$).

Substitute in (1): $a(1 - 2) = -5$, so $a = 5$.

**Check.** The terms are $5,\ -10,\ 20,\ -40,\ 80$. First plus second $= 5 - 10 = -5$. Fourth plus fifth $= -40 + 80 = 40$.

$$\boxed{a = 5,\quad r = -2}$$

questions.enonce_markdown: Find the term independent of $x$ in the expansion of $\left(x + \dfrac{2}{x^2}\right)^{15}$. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The general term (the $(k+1)$th term) of the binomial expansion is

$$T_{k+1} = \binom{15}{k} x^{15-k}\left(\frac{2}{x^2}\right)^{k} = \binom{15}{k}\, 2^k\, x^{15 - k - 2k} = \binom{15}{k}\, 2^k\, x^{15 - 3k}.$$

The term is independent of $x$ when the power of $x$ is $0$: $15 - 3k = 0$, so $k = 5$. This is the 6th term.

$$T_6 = \binom{15}{5} 2^5 = 3003 \times 32 = 96096.$$

$$\boxed{\text{The term independent of } x \text{ is } 96\,096}$$

($\binom{15}{5} = \dfrac{15 \cdot 14 \cdot 13 \cdot 12 \cdot 11}{5!} = 3003$.)
